content:
Nuevo Laredo is rolling out the red carpet for its ranching roots. The city government is inviting families to the 2nd Fat Calf Contest — the “2.º Concurso del Novillo Gordo” — with final weigh-in and awards set for Saturday, Oct. 24, at the Rastro Municipal, according to Periódico Valle Del Norte.

The event, organized through the city’s Rural Development office under the Secretariat of Economic Development, is a full day built around the region’s livestock tradition. Exhibitors must bring their animals in between 8 and 11 a.m.; the day’s activities start at noon at the Rastro Municipal on General Francisco Munguía street in the Hipódromo neighborhood.

Beyond the weigh-in itself, attendees can expect live music, carne asada, prizes and surprises, in what the city describes as a space for family gathering and for sharing the traditions and togetherness that are part of Nuevo Laredo’s rural identity. The final weigh-in and awards ceremony are the centerpiece, recognizing the participating producers under the contest’s format.

City officials say gatherings like this aim to give visibility to ranching work and keep alive participatory spaces that preserve the traditions of the rural sector — while bringing producers and residents together face to face.
